question: Can a local temporal-curvature penalty reshape a JEPA world model's visual latent space so that Euclidean goal distance and gradient-based action optimization become more reliable than planning in frozen pretrained features?

key_findings.claim: The proposed intervention is a two-term JEPA objective that predicts the next latent while maximizing the cosine similarity of consecutive latent displacement vectors.
key_findings.evidence: The sensory encoder, action encoder, and causal ViT predictor are trained jointly with next-latent MSE against a stop-gradient target plus L_curv = 1 - cos(z_{t+1}-z_t, z_{t+2}-z_{t+1}). The main spatial implementation applies the curvature term after a learned 128-dimensional aggregation head while retaining spatial tokens for prediction and planning.

key_findings.claim: The conditioning theorem is valid for the paper's linear terminal-cost model, but it does not establish the claimed nonlinear planning effect or the fidelity of Euclidean distance to geodesic distance.
key_findings.evidence: For z_{t+1}=Az_t+Ba_t, the nonzero Hessian spectrum equals that of the finite-horizon controllability Gramian, and the paper derives kappa_eff(H) <= kappa(B)^2((1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon))^{2(K-1)} when epsilon=||A-I||_2<1. The paper explicitly leaves nonlinear predictors to future work. Its practical cosine proxy additionally assumes constant velocity magnitudes and smooth actions, controls A-I only along visited velocity directions, and needs an untested coverage condition to become a spectral bound. No experiment measures A, epsilon, a Hessian condition number, or a geodesic-distortion statistic.

C.3 / Assumption C.7 and Proposition C.9

key_findings.claim: On the strongest spatial DINOv2-projector setup, explicit straightening produces large short-horizon gains, especially on UMaze.
key_findings.evidence: Across 50 test episodes and three evaluation-data seeds, adding L_curv to 14x14x8 projected DINOv2 features changes open-loop/MPC success from 80.00/90.67 to 90.67/100.00 on Wall, 44.00/81.33 to 94.00/100.00 on UMaze, 72.00/96.67 to 82.67/98.67 on Medium, and 70.00/78.67 to 77.33/85.33 on PushT. These are absolute percentage-point changes, not relative percentages.

key_findings.claim: The spatial ResNet comparison is dramatic but also reveals that the no-curvature representation can catastrophically degrade on three navigation tasks.
key_findings.evidence: For the 14x14x8 ResNet, straightening changes open-loop/MPC success from 1.33/6.67 to 84.67/100.00 on Wall, 14.67/66.00 to 64.67/98.67 on UMaze, and 18.67/57.33 to 80.67/99.33 on Medium. On PushT, however, open-loop success slightly falls from 71.33 to 70.67 while MPC rises from 70.67 to 91.33. Thus the evidence is as much a rescue from a failed no-curvature training condition as a uniformly incremental planning improvement.

key_findings.claim: The main straightening ablation is confounded by a learning-rate change chosen after observing severe no-curvature degradation.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix Table 3 lists a 1e-5 spatial projector/ResNet learning rate, but its footnote states that training without straightening severely degraded performance and therefore uses 1e-6 for the no-straightening condition. Since curvature and learning rate change together in the central comparisons, the tables do not isolate the causal contribution of L_curv; no crossed lambda-by-learning-rate ablation is reported.

key_findings.claim: The paper's statement that straightening consistently improves both GD and CEM is contradicted by its own planner table.
key_findings.evidence: For projected DINOv2 on Medium, CEM success decreases from 92.67 to 86.67 after adding curvature; for the spatial ResNet on PushT, GD decreases from 71.33 to 70.67. Most other cells improve, including projected-DINO UMaze GD from 44.00 to 94.00 and CEM from 75.33 to 94.00, but the universal wording is false. CEM uses 200 samples x 10 iterations and is reported roughly 10x slower than 100-step GD on one L40S GPU.

key_findings.claim: Long-horizon results show compounding-model-error limits and several non-improvements from curvature or the combined cost.
key_findings.evidence: At 50-step goals, PushT projected-DINO MPC falls from 26.67 without curvature to 24.00 with curvature, and ResNet open-loop falls from 13.33 to 10.67, although both straightened models remain above frozen DINO-WM open-loop at 3.33. On Medium, straightened ResNet reaches 76.00 open-loop and 98.67 MPC versus 14.67/48.00 without curvature. Adding 0.1 times an aggregated global cost improves PushT MPC to 33.33 or 36.00 and projected-DINO Medium MPC to 92.00, but reduces Medium open-loop from 68.00 to 66.67 for the projector and from 76.00 to 68.67 for ResNet; ResNet Medium MPC stays 98.67 rather than improving. Figure 9 explicitly shows imagined-rollout drift and blur.

key_findings.claim: The claimed Euclidean-to-geodesic alignment is visually suggestive but not quantitatively established.
key_findings.evidence: Maze heatmaps and PCA trajectories look more transition-aware after straightening, and detached VAE decodings appear visually faithful even from compressed latents. However, the paper reports no correlation, rank error, shortest-path distortion, reconstruction metric, or uncertainty over these visualizations. A-star grids also abstract away PointMaze velocity and inertia, so they are not exact geodesics of the full simulator state.

key_findings.claim: Moderate channel compression and a learned global aggregation head are the strongest design choices, but their ablations are not coefficient-matched.
key_findings.evidence: Keeping 196 patches while reducing DINOv2 channels from 384 to 8 or 32 works best; 2 channels underfit and 128 can hurt planning. All four spatial cosine variants outperform no straightening in the reported plots, with the learned 128-dimensional aggregation head best. Yet the aggregation variant uses lambda=0.1 while patch, mean, and flatten use lambda=0.01, each selected for best performance, so the head comparison jointly changes operator and regularization strength.

key_findings.claim: Smoothness and temporal contrastive regularization are reported as negative baselines, but only on one environment and without tabulated values.
key_findings.evidence: On 50 PushT episodes over three data seeds, increasing either regularizer reportedly hurts and no tested weight matches curvature straightening. The comparison does not cover the three navigation environments, and Figure 12 rather than a numeric table carries the result, limiting exact effect-size auditing.

key_findings.claim: The Teleported-PointMaze example demonstrates the intended transition-aware behavior only qualitatively and also exposes the symmetric-cost limitation.
key_findings.evidence: A one-way right-to-left teleport makes pixel-near and transition-near relations disagree. One illustrated straightened trajectory uses the teleport while the no-curvature planner gets stuck, and the heatmap is closer to A-star. There is no episode-level success rate or multi-seed statistic, and the authors acknowledge that symmetric MSE cannot represent directional reachability.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation is broad enough to show a repeatable 2D benchmark trend but too small and curated to establish general latent-planning reliability.
key_findings.evidence: Training uses 1,920 Wall trajectories, 2,000 UMaze, 4,000 Medium, and 18,500 PushT trajectories. Test starts and goals are sampled from held-out trajectories specifically to guarantee reachability within 25 simulator steps. Each table cell uses 50 episodes and three evaluation-data seeds; global-feature lambda is selected by MPC on only two validation seeds. There are no real-robot, 3D, stochastic-observation, discrete-action, or out-of-distribution goal tests.

key_findings.claim: Stop-gradient does not theoretically rule out representation collapse, and the paper supplies no direct collapse or information-sufficiency measurement.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly state that a collapsing solution remains possible in theory and rely on prior empirical success of stop-gradient. Their own information check is a detached decoder and visual reconstructions rather than latent variance, rank, mutual information, task-state identifiability, or quantitative reconstruction error. This matters because curvature can be minimized by suppressing state variation.

method.core_idea: Fine-tune or learn a visual encoder together with a JEPA latent dynamics predictor while penalizing changes in direction between adjacent latent velocities, then optimize continuous action sequences directly through the learned model with latent MSE to a goal.
method.mechanism: Observations become spatial or global visual latents; actions and optional proprioception are embedded and supplied to a causally masked ViT predictor. A stop-gradient next-latent MSE supplies predictability, while one minus cosine similarity of successive latent differences supplies local temporal straightness. For spatial tokens, a learned 128-dimensional aggregation head receives the curvature loss while prediction stays spatial. At test time Adam differentiates a terminal or weighted trajectory-to-goal loss through five learned rollout steps corresponding to 25 simulator steps; MPC executes one frame-skipped action chunk and replans. The analysis relates A near identity in a linear latent system to a better-conditioned controllability Gramian and uses strong auxiliary assumptions to connect velocity cosine to A-I along observed directions.
assumptions: Three-frame local straightness is an adequate surrogate for globally useful goal geometry and does not create latent shortcuts between dynamically disconnected states.
Cosine similarity should ignore velocity magnitude, even though the theory's proxy proposition assumes all latent velocities have the same norm.
Training actions are smooth enough that B(a_{t+1}-a_t) does not dominate changes in latent velocity.
Visited velocity directions cover the relevant latent subspace sufficiently to turn directional control of A-I into something resembling spectral control; this coverage is not measured.
A nonlinear ViT predictor behaves sufficiently like the linear time-invariant model z_{t+1}=Az_t+Ba_t for the Hessian argument to explain optimization.
A transition matrix near identity is desirable across tasks; rapidly rotating, oscillatory, contact-switching, or hybrid dynamics may not admit such coordinates without losing information.
A symmetric Euclidean terminal cost captures reachability, despite explicitly asymmetric teleportation and other irreversible dynamics.
A-star distance over a positional grid is a valid geodesic reference for PointMaze despite velocity, acceleration, and inertia in the simulator state.
Stop-gradient plus prediction prevents collapse well enough without an explicit variance, covariance, contrastive, or reconstruction constraint.
Changing the no-curvature spatial learning rate from 1e-5 to 1e-6 does not materially confound attribution to the regularizer.
Fifty reachable, trajectory-sampled test goals and three data seeds adequately estimate planning reliability.
Frame-skip-five rollouts preserve the dynamics needed for contact-rich PushT and do not hide intermediate collisions or regime switches.
The terminal-only Hessian's effective nonzero condition number is the relevant optimizer difficulty even though the action-space Hessian has a large nullspace when horizon exceeds latent dimension.
Action bounds, clipping, and Adam's non-quadratic behavior do not invalidate conclusions drawn from unconstrained gradient descent on a quadratic terminal loss.

techniques.role: Penalizes turns between consecutive encoded trajectory displacements without negative samples.
Learns future visual features rather than reconstructing pixels.
Blocks target-branch gradients as the sole main anti-collapse mechanism.
Compresses frozen DINOv2 patch channels from 384 to as few as 8 while preserving 14x14 spatial layout.
Maps moving/occluded patch features to a global 128-dimensional trajectory feature for the curvature loss.
Autoregressively predicts spatial latents from a three-frame state/action history.
Backpropagates latent goal loss through imagined rollouts and updates continuous actions with Adam.
Executes the first frame-skipped action chunk, observes the new state, and optimizes again.
Expresses the terminal-cost Hessian's nonzero spectrum through a finite-horizon linear-system Gramian.
Qualitatively compares learned Euclidean distance fields with positional shortest-path maps.
Breaks visual proximity with a one-way transition to test whether the representation tracks experienced dynamics.

evaluations.setting: Wall with 1,920 offline trajectories of 50 steps; 50 reachable test episodes, three evaluation-data seeds, frame skip 5.
evaluations.result: Spatial DINOv2+projector improves from 80.00+/-7.12 to 90.67+/-0.94 open-loop and 90.67+/-3.77 to 100.00+/-0.00 MPC with curvature; spatial ResNet improves from 1.33+/-1.89 to 84.67+/-2.49 and 6.67+/-1.89 to 100.00+/-0.00.
evaluations.baseline: The same reported encoder family without L_curv, plus frozen DINOv2 patch features at 52.67+/-5.73 open-loop and 76.67+/-6.18 MPC.

evaluations.setting: PointMaze-UMaze with 2,000 offline trajectories of 100 steps; 50 reachable test episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: Spatial DINOv2+projector rises from 44.00+/-7.12 to 94.00+/-1.63 open-loop and 81.33+/-6.80 to 100.00+/-0.00 MPC; spatial ResNet rises from 14.67+/-4.99 to 64.67+/-8.38 and 66.00+/-9.09 to 98.67+/-1.89.
evaluations.baseline: Matched reported no-curvature models and frozen DINOv2 patch features at 35.33+/-4.11 open-loop and 80.67+/-6.18 MPC.

evaluations.setting: PointMaze-Medium with 4,000 offline trajectories of 100 steps; 50 reachable test episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: Spatial DINOv2+projector changes 72.00+/-4.32 to 82.67+/-3.77 open-loop and 96.67+/-0.94 to 98.67+/-0.94 MPC; spatial ResNet changes 18.67+/-4.11 to 80.67+/-0.94 and 57.33+/-4.71 to 99.33+/-0.94.
evaluations.baseline: Matched reported no-curvature models and frozen DINOv2 patch features at 40.83+/-10.07 open-loop and 76.67+/-5.14 MPC.

evaluations.setting: PushT with 18,500 offline trajectories of length 100-300; 50 reachable test episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: Spatial DINOv2+projector changes 70.00+/-1.63 to 77.33+/-6.18 open-loop and 78.67+/-0.94 to 85.33+/-4.99 MPC. Spatial ResNet open-loop changes 71.33+/-7.36 to 70.67+/-0.94, while MPC rises 70.67+/-10.50 to 91.33+/-2.49.
evaluations.baseline: Matched reported no-curvature models and frozen DINOv2 patch features at 56.00+/-4.32 open-loop and 66.00+/-4.90 MPC.

evaluations.setting: Global 1x384 representations across Wall, UMaze, Medium, and PushT.
evaluations.result: Straightened ResNet global features outperform their no-curvature versions in all eight cells, including Wall 58.67/68.00 to 86.67/97.33 and PushT 40.00/70.00 to 58.67/83.33. The DINOv2 global projector is mixed: PushT MPC decreases 11.33 to 8.67 and open-loop stays 2.00.
evaluations.baseline: DINOv2 CLS, frozen-patch global projector without curvature, and global ResNet without curvature.

evaluations.setting: Open-loop GD versus CEM with spatial features; CEM uses 200 samples and 10 iterations, GD uses 100 Adam steps.
evaluations.metric: Success rate over 50 trajectories, three data seeds, and wall-clock planning time on one L40S GPU.
evaluations.result: CEM is roughly 10x slower and often more successful; curvature closes much of the gap. Counterexamples are projected-DINO Medium CEM 92.67 to 86.67 and ResNet PushT GD 71.33 to 70.67 after curvature.
evaluations.baseline: The same model with the alternative planner and no-curvature versions.

evaluations.setting: Longer 50-step goals on PushT and PointMaze-Medium with spatial features.
evaluations.result: Straightened projector/ResNet score 13.33/24.00 and 10.67/33.33 on PushT, and 68.00/88.00 and 76.00/98.67 on Medium. A combined spatial+0.1 aggregated cost raises PushT MPC to 33.33/36.00 and projector Medium MPC to 92.00, but some open-loop cells fall.
evaluations.baseline: Frozen DINO-WM at PushT 3.33/27.33 and Medium 35.00/65.33, plus each learned encoder without curvature.

evaluations.setting: DINOv2 spatial-projector channel dimension in {2, 8, 32, 128}, evaluated by open-loop GD on four environments.
evaluations.metric: Success rate across 50 episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: Two channels are insufficient, 8 or 32 generally perform best, and 128 can reduce success; exact plot values are not tabulated.
evaluations.baseline: The 384-channel frozen patch representation and other compressed widths.

evaluations.setting: Patch, mean-pooled, flattened, and learned-aggregation cosine variants on the DINOv2 196x8 projector.
evaluations.metric: Open-loop success over 50 episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: All plotted variants improve over no curvature, with the learned 128-dimensional aggregation head best; aggregation uses lambda=0.1 while the other variants use lambda=0.01.
evaluations.baseline: No curvature and three fixed aggregation operators.

evaluations.setting: Smoothness and temporal-contrastive regularizers on PushT with the frozen-DINOv2 spatial projector.
evaluations.metric: Open-loop GD success over 50 episodes and three seeds.
evaluations.result: Neither regularizer improves the reported result; larger weights hurt more, while curvature is best in the plot.
evaluations.baseline: No temporal regularizer and temporal straightening.

evaluations.setting: PointMaze and PushT representation diagnostics using PCA trajectories, A-star distance heatmaps, and a detached VAE decoder.
evaluations.result: Straightened trajectories appear smoother, distance heatmaps more shortest-path-like, and decoded frames visually faithful; no quantitative geodesic or reconstruction score is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Frozen DINOv2 CLS/patch features and learned encoders without curvature.

evaluations.metric: Qualitative distance heatmap and representative planning trajectory.
evaluations.result: The straightened planner uses the teleport and reaches the target in the shown case while the no-curvature planner gets stuck; no aggregate success statistic is supplied.
evaluations.baseline: DINOv2 patch embeddings, projector without curvature, and A-star positional distance.

limitations: Author-stated: the method currently addresses continuous goal-conditioned planning with a symmetric Euclidean cost, which can be suboptimal for asymmetric or irreversible dynamics.
Author-stated: long-horizon prediction errors compound, causing imagined trajectory drift, blur, and simulator mismatch.
Author-stated: nonlinear conditioning guarantees are left for future work because they require control of state-dependent Jacobian products and higher-order terms.
Author-stated: a collapsing encoder remains possible in theory despite stop-gradient.
Reviewer-identified: the central no-curvature spatial condition uses a different learning rate, so the regularizer's causal effect is not isolated.
Reviewer-identified: the cosine-to-conditioning bridge assumes constant velocity magnitude, smooth actions, and direction coverage, none of which is measured or enforced.
Reviewer-identified: no Hessian spectrum, A-I norm, optimizer-convergence curve, or nonlinear analogue validates the proposed theoretical mechanism.
Reviewer-identified: the effective Hessian condition number discards a large action-space nullspace and does not address box constraints, clipping, Adam, or nonunique action solutions.
Reviewer-identified: geodesic fidelity is judged from heatmaps and PCA rather than quantified distortion; A-star position grids omit velocity and inertia.
Reviewer-identified: the phrase 'consistently improves both GD and CEM' conflicts with at least two cells in Table 5.
Reviewer-identified: straightening decreases some short- and long-horizon cells, including ResNet PushT open-loop and projected-DINO PushT long-horizon MPC.
Reviewer-identified: cosine-variant comparisons tune different lambda values, so the aggregation-head effect is not isolated.
Reviewer-identified: smoothness and temporal-contrastive negative baselines are tested only on PushT and reported only graphically.
Reviewer-identified: Teleported-PointMaze has only a representative trajectory, not an aggregate evaluation, and symmetric MSE cannot encode its directional reachability.
Reviewer-identified: starts and goals are sampled from held-out trajectories to be reachable within 25 steps, narrowing difficulty and distribution shift.
Reviewer-identified: only four visually simple 2D simulator tasks are tested; no physical robot, 3D scene, stochastic partial observation, discrete action, or safety constraint is evaluated.
Reviewer-identified: 50 episodes, three evaluation-data seeds, and two validation seeds are modest for hyperparameter-sensitive planning.
Reviewer-identified: information preservation is supported by visual decodes but not reconstruction error, latent variance/rank, state identifiability, or behaviorally relevant sufficiency.
Reviewer-identified: the planner-horizon description alternates between 25 actions and H=5 predictor rollouts under frame skip five, leaving action-chunk semantics insufficiently explicit.
failure_modes: Curvature minimization can collapse or overcompress the representation, making different controllable states indistinguishable while achieving a low loss.
A visually straight latent trajectory can create Euclidean shortcuts across walls or between states with different velocity, contact mode, or directional reachability.
Abrupt but necessary turns, oscillations, rotations, contact switches, and hybrid transitions can be penalized as undesirable curvature.
Sparse trajectory coverage can straighten only observed directions, leaving novel goals or action-induced directions ill-conditioned.
Model error compounds over long rollouts, so a smooth latent cost can guide optimization toward actions whose imagined endpoint is infeasible in the simulator.
Symmetric terminal MSE can recommend the wrong direction or get stuck in irreversible systems such as the one-way teleport environment.
A global feature can smooth long-range distance but erase local contact or obstacle detail; spatial tokens can preserve detail while yielding a rough optimization landscape.
Gradient descent can converge to one of many action-space null directions or hit action bounds even when the nonzero linear Hessian spectrum is well conditioned.
Learning-rate sensitivity can make the no-curvature model fail, exaggerating the apparent benefit of the geometric loss.
CEM or MPC can outperform open-loop gradient descent through replanning/search even when the representation itself has not acquired globally correct geometry.
Two-frame velocities with very small norms make cosine estimates numerically unstable unless explicitly stabilized.
A detached decoder can reconstruct superficial appearance while the control-relevant state remains aliased.
reusable_insights: Evaluate latent planning geometry separately at three levels: local trajectory curvature, global directed shortest-path distortion, and actual optimizer convergence.
When regularizing spatial video features, separate the prediction representation from a learned global geometry head rather than forcing patch identities to remain temporally aligned.
Cross learning rate with regularizer strength; a no-regularizer run rescued by a smaller learning rate is an essential causal control, not merely a training detail.
Report every negative planner cell and distinguish absolute percentage-point gains from relative-percent gains.
For irreversible dynamics, learn a directional quasimetric or value-conditioned goal cost rather than symmetric Euclidean distance.
Test representation geometry with transition interventions that decouple visual similarity from temporal reachability, but use aggregate statistics rather than a single trajectory.
A terminal-loss conditioning theorem should report nullspace dimension, action constraints, and convergence on the controllable subspace.
Combine fine spatial costs with smoother global costs for long horizons, then validate whether the mix helps closed-loop and open-loop planning separately.
Straightness should be normalized against speed variation and action curvature if it is to approximate an A-near-identity condition.
Use nonlinear low-loss-landscape diagnostics or measured rollout Jacobians before attributing empirical gains to a linear Gramian bound.
open_questions: Do gains remain after a full crossed ablation of learning rate, lambda, encoder capacity, and anti-collapse method?
Does straightening measurably reduce the condition number of the actual nonlinear action-loss Hessian or rollout Jacobian on successful plans?
Can a directed quasimetric retain the optimization benefits while representing teleportation, friction, contacts, and other irreversible dynamics?
How much trajectory-direction coverage is required before local cosine straightness generalizes to unseen state-action directions?
Would curvature weighted by latent speed or controlled for action acceleration better match the theorem's assumptions?
Can variance/covariance regularization prevent collapse without sacrificing the low-dimensional planning geometry?
How does the method compare under identical compute and hyperparameter tuning with PCC-style dynamics curvature, temporal contrastive inference, and prior straightening objectives?
Does the method scale to 3D manipulation, real images, multimodal futures, partial observability, and discrete or hybrid action spaces?
Can global geodesic distortion, directed reachability error, and reconstruction/state-identification error be quantified rather than visualized?
Why does explicit curvature reduce performance in specific PushT and Medium planner cells, and are those differences statistically significant?
How should the goal cost adapt when spatial and aggregated representations disagree?
Does an online or actively collected dataset target missing velocity directions and improve global conditioning more efficiently than passive offline trajectories?

competitive_landscape.title: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
competitive_landscape.relationship: The exact frozen-feature latent world-model baseline and data/planning protocol on which Temporal Straightening builds.
competitive_landscape.difference: DINO-WM predicts frozen DINOv2 spatial features and relies chiefly on test-time search; the reviewed paper trains a projector or encoder with an explicit temporal-curvature term and emphasizes gradient-based planning. It therefore improves representation geometry but inherits DINO-WM's offline 2D benchmark scope.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 267, ICML 2025 proceedings edition, pages 79115-79135 (conference dates 2025-07-13 to 2025-07-19)

competitive_landscape.title: Prediction, Consistency, Curvature: Representation Learning for Locally-Linear Control
competitive_landscape.relationship: A direct earlier representation-learning method that jointly uses prediction, consistency, and a curvature penalty to make high-dimensional observations amenable to latent control.
competitive_landscape.difference: PCC penalizes second-order curvature of the learned latent transition function and plans with locally linear control/iLQR in a variational latent model; Temporal Straightening penalizes the observed trajectory's adjacent velocity angle inside a JEPA and plans by backpropagating a goal loss. PCC substantially narrows any claim that curvature for latent planning is new.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2020 published conference-paper edition, OpenReview forum BJxG_0EtDS

competitive_landscape.title: Learning predictable and robust neural representations by straightening image sequences
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest prior explicit straightening objective for visual sequences, using temporal trajectory geometry as a self-supervised representation-learning principle.
competitive_landscape.difference: Niu et al. study predictability, factorization, noise robustness, and adversarial robustness on rendered sequences, not action-conditioned world models or goal planning. The reviewed paper's narrower novelty is the JEPA world-model/planning deployment and its conditioning analysis, not straightening itself.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 proceedings, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, Main Conference Track, DOI 10.52202/079017-1275

competitive_landscape.title: Inference via Interpolation: Contrastive Representations Provably Enable Planning and Inference
competitive_landscape.relationship: A direct alternative for learning temporal representation geometry in which prediction and planning reduce to compact Gaussian inference and, in a special case, interpolation.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives a Gauss-Markov structure from a temporal contrastive objective and validates numerical tasks up to 46 dimensions; Temporal Straightening avoids negatives, targets adjacent velocity angles, learns action-conditioned visual dynamics, and evaluates simulator control. The contrastive method has stronger probabilistic structure but different data and planner assumptions.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 proceedings, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, Main Conference Track, DOI 10.52202/079017-1878

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Linearize Under Uncertainty
competitive_landscape.relationship: An early visual-representation method that explicitly linearizes short temporal trajectories and includes a cosine straightening term while handling multiple possible futures.
competitive_landscape.difference: Goroshin et al. use a generative frame-prediction architecture and latent uncertainty on video rather than a joint-embedding action-conditioned world model or downstream latent goal planner. It establishes that the local cosine mechanism predates the reviewed paper by more than a decade.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NIPS 2015 proceedings, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 28

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim that prior straightening work did not study its effect on world modeling and planning, and present temporal straightening as a simple geometry regularizer that makes Euclidean latent distance more geodesic, improves the conditioning of gradient-based planning, and raises open-loop and MPC success by roughly 20-60% and 20-30% across goal-reaching tasks.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines a JEPA predictor with adjacent-velocity cosine regularization, a learned aggregation head for spatial features, a linear controllability-Gramian bound, four offline 2D goal-reaching benchmarks, a long-horizon study, and a one-way teleport stress test. Direct primary records show that cosine trajectory linearization existed in NIPS 2015, explicit straightening representation learning in NeurIPS 2024, and curvature-regularized latent control in ICLR 2020; DINO-WM supplies the immediate world-model baseline.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the specific integration of local temporal straightening with a JEPA visual world model, spatial/global feature handling, differentiable goal planning, and a targeted 2D empirical evaluation. It is not the first temporal straightening loss, the first curvature-aware latent representation, or the first curvature regularizer motivated by control. The theory is a scoped explanatory model rather than a guarantee for the implemented nonlinear system, and the learning-rate confound plus several negative cells weaken causal and universal claims.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 29-page extracted text, including Appendix A data, Appendix B hyperparameters and all ablations, Appendix C proofs and proxy assumptions, Appendix D extended related work, Appendix E visualizations, and Appendix F Teleported-PointMaze. Anchors were checked against page delimiters in the extracted text. Provenance fields are copied exactly from data/generated/fulltext_index.jsonl and use primary-full-text-v1. Competitor identities, exact titles, and fixed official editions were checked on 2026-08-23 against PMLR, OpenReview, and NeurIPS primary pages. This is a first-pass full-text reading, not a second-review verification. The most consequential audit findings are the 1e-5 versus 1e-6 no-curvature learning-rate confound, theory-to-practice assumption gap, unquantified geodesic claims, and planner cells that contradict 'consistent' improvement wording.
